# dsh-vps-ops
Read-first VPS operations tools for DeepSeek Harness.

`dsh-vps-ops` gives your DSH agent a small, explicit toolkit for running a
server: systemd status, d

isk usage, Docker status, log tails, configured
backups, and quiet-hours schedule checks. Nothing ab

out your host is baked into
the code — every unit, container, backup command, and time window comes

ked into
the code — every unit, container, backup command, and time window comes from
plugin config.

**Read-only by default.** Destructive tools refuse in read-only mode, only
accept allow-listed targe
ts, and ask the host for approval before running.
## Tools
| Tool | Kind | What it does |
| `service_status` | read-only | `systemctl` state, sub-state, restarts, PID, start time, host uptim

e, last error journal lines. One configured unit or all of them. |
| `disk_usage` | read-only | `df

-h /`, inode usage, and the five largest top-level directories under `/`. |
| `docker_status` | read
-only | Running containers, or `docker inspect` state/health/restarts for one configured container.

|
| `log_tail` | read-only | `journalctl` tail for a configured unit, or the tail of an absolute fil

e inside the configured log directories. Max 200 lines. |
| `quiet_hours_status` | read-only | Pure
schedule calculation: lists the windows and says whether *now* is inside one. Starts and stops nothi

ng. |
| `service_action` | destructive | `systemctl start|stop|restart` for one configured unit, aft

er approval. |
| `backup_run` | destructive | Runs one operator-configured backup command, after app

val. |
| `backup_run` | destructive | Runs one operator-configured backup command, after approval. |

## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `services` | `[]` | `{ label, unit }` allow-list of systemd units. |
| `containers` | `[]` | `{ la

bel, name }` allow-list of Docker containers. |
| `backups` | `[]` | `{ id, label, command, timeoutM

s }`; `command` is an argv array (preferred) or a shell string. |
| `quietHours.timeZone` | `UTC` |

IANA zone used to evaluate the windows. |
| `quietHours.windows` | `[]` | `"<days> HH:MM-HH:MM"`; da

y ranges may wrap (`Fri-Mon`) and a window whose end precedes its start crosses midnight. |
| `logs.

dirs` | `["/var/log"]` | Directories `log_tail` may read files from. |
| `audit.file` | `<DSH_HOME>/

logs/vps-ops-audit.log` | Where approved operations are recorded. |
| `safety.readOnly` | `true` | W

hen true, `service_action` and `backup_run` refuse. |
| `safety.requireApproval` | `true` | When tru

e, destructive tools ask the host first. |
| `safety.timeoutMs` | `15000` | Default command timeout.

|
| `safety.maxOutputBytes` | `65536` | Output cap per call. |
## Safety model

- **No shell interpolation of model input.** Commands are executed as an
executable plus an argv arr

ay. Names are validated before they reach an argv
slot, which also blocks option injection such as a

unit called `--help`.
- **Allow-lists only.** `service_action`, `docker_status <container>`,
`log_t

ail <unit>`, and `backup_run` accept only configured names.
- **Files stay in the log directories.**

`log_tail <file>` resolves symlinks and
refuses anything outside `logs.dirs`.
- **Bounded work.** E

very command has a wall-clock timeout and a stdout/stderr
byte cap; runaway output kills the child.

- **No secret plumbing.** Children get a minimal environment, and no tool reads
or forwards credenti

als.
- **Fail-closed approval.** A missing or throwing approval answerer means the
operation does no

t run.
- **One audit line per approved operation**, as JSON on a single line.
## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.1-rc.4` (Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`).
- `systemctl` / `journalctl` for the systemd to

ols, `docker` for the Docker tool.
Missing binaries are reported as tool output, not as crashes.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The suite covers window parsing and evaluation, argv building, UTF-8 safe output
truncation, output

parsers, and the destructive-operation gate (read-only
refusal, rejected approval, missing answerer,
approved execution, audit line).
